text:
Bobby Brink's first full season in Minnesota, after 201 games in Philadelphia, is quietly working. The Wild won seven of his last ten games, and he's settled on a line with Blake Coleman and Mike McCarron that scored twice against Utah on Wednesday, as Heather Rule noted, with Brink cleaning up a power-play rebound for one of them. The Duluth News Tribune wrote that he "finds another level to his game during recent road trip."

The numbers say he's helping more than his 12 points show. Minnesota gets 56% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him on, almost five points better than without him, and he has 3 goals on 5.2 expected, shooting 7.5% against a talent range closer to 11 to 15%. Those looks usually start going in.

The cap on his production is ice time: 13:23 a night, under 11 minutes in each of his last two games. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming from defense, which fits a winger playing a checking role.

He's a 25-year-old Minnesota native doing useful work for a team that's winning. More goals would make it obvious.
headline: Bobby Brink, finding a role in Minnesota
